chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you pray an obligatory prayer, pray it for its time, as a farewell prayer, fearing that you will not return to it ever. Then direct your gaze to the place of your prostration. If you knew who is on your right and left, you would perfect your prayer. And know that you are before One who sees you and you do not see Him.
ai.seo_question: How should one focus during obligatory prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the obligatory prayer (*fard*) by urging believers to pray it with the intensity of a farewell prayer (*salat al-mudhi*), recognizing the uncertainty of life. He further refines the concept of *khushu'* (focus) by directing the gaze to the place of prostration and linking it to the psychological awareness of God's omniscience, a theme deeply rooted in Shia spiritual psychology. This instruction underscores that true perfection in prayer arises not just from ritual correctness, but from the internal realization that one is constantly observed by the Divine.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  says,  “O  Abdullah,  when  you offer an obligatory prayer, offer it on time. Else it is possible that  you  might  lose  the  opportunity  to  do  so.  Focus  your eyes on the place of your prostrations while offering Salaat. You pray carefully as if there is someone around you. Know that He is seeing you and you are not able to see Him.”
